- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days); cap forecast at 10-15% above recent peak.
- In mean-reversion regimes (sentiment neutral or mixed), model often fails to correct downward; apply mild downward bias if price has been rising for 5+ days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out abrupt changes in forecast slope.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model may overcorrect; reduce forecast by 2-5% to avoid “sentiment-driven overbought” traps.
- When sentiment is low and price is rising, model often underestimates upside; add 3-5% buffer if sentiment <0.3 and price > previous 5-day high.
